projects.name: License Plate Reader Investigation
projects.tagline: Ten cameras in one Utah county were searched 5.1 million times by police in 45 states. Records show 41.4% of searches carry a stated reason that matches no purpose Utah law permits.

articles.headline: Most of this Utah county's license plate camera data is searched by out-of-state law enforcement
articles.excerpt: Records obtained by Utah Civic Compact show ten Flock Safety cameras in Weber County were searched 5.1 million times between February 2022 and July 2026, with almost 97% of those searches coming from agencies outside Utah. The Houston Police Department alone accounted for more than a third of all activity.

articles.headline: Group cites 'striking' Weber County data on Flock cameras as reason for lawmakers to act
articles.excerpt: Utah Civic Compact released public records at the Capitol showing Weber County's license plate reader cameras were searched more than 5 million times since early 2022, overwhelmingly by out-of-state agencies. The group is calling on state lawmakers to tighten the rules governing how outside agencies access Utah data.

projects.name: Stratos Project
projects.tagline: Fighting MIDA's unlawful approval of a 9-gigawatt natural gas data center in Hansel Valley.

articles.headline: MIDA violated state law in approval process of Box Elder County data center, group claims
articles.excerpt: Utah Civic Compact released a detailed briefing alleging that the Military Installation Development Authority broke three provisions of state law in fast-tracking approval of the Stratos Project — a proposed 9-gigawatt natural gas data center in Hansel Valley backed by Kevin O'Leary.

articles.headline: Data center official counters worries about project footprint; foes raise new concerns
articles.excerpt: O'Leary Digital's CEO argues the proposed Hansel Valley development will occupy a limited footprint with most land preserved as open space, while Utah Civic Compact challenges whether state officials followed proper legal procedures in approving the controversial project.
